theme_note: These codes hold together because participants allocate pixels between extending the patterned edge and repairing or filling what they already hold. What varies is the chosen priority, direction, perimeter strategy, and whether a cleaner openly disobeys expansion-first instructions.

These codes recruit, welcome, convert, or declare belonging to the lattice and spread its public message. They vary from practical invitations and promoted posts to mock-religious conversion language, pride, and movement between green groups.

These codes work out how lattice growth can share space with art, flags, coloured groups, and allies. The practice ranges from treaties and safe passage to build-around rules, requests for protection, disputed boundaries, and exchanges of help.

These codes mobilize against swastikas, rival colours, invasions, rumours of backing, and calls to attack. What varies is whether the threat is verified, later covered by a treaty, or framed as a wider danger to canvas communities.

second_order: organizing through rules, cross-posts, and Discord
theme_note: These codes make coordination infrastructure: cross-posting strategy, opening and advertising Discord, publishing rules, and asking how the interface works. They differ in venue and form but all make dispersed pixel work actionable.

These codes make the group findable on the canvas by proposing, locating, building, marking, repairing, and celebrating its sign. Variation lies in design work, recruitment, mistaken erasure, and near-completion.
These codes ask the lattice itself for permission to add a picture inside its grid. The proposed images differ, while the shared practice is treating the lattice as a place able to admit art.

second_order: celebrating and joking about the lattice
theme_note: These codes make the lattice enjoyable and recognizable through praise, visual jokes, reaction images, and wordplay. They vary from calling the view beautiful to recasting ordinary images and repeating an action-image joke.

These codes concern art already being made inside lattice territory: reminding cleaners that it is permitted, defending it from green pixels, completing it, and thanking its builders. What varies is the project and whether permission has reached ordinary placers.
This single code belongs with no other slice-02 practice: it asks participants to abstain from coloured placement altogether because colour is framed as violence.

second_order: ruling on what may be built inside
theme_note: These codes draw and apply the lattice's admission boundary for new work. They vary between refusing new art, redirecting applicants elsewhere or to diplomacy, defining a clean core, and requiring builders to ask first.

second_order: changing the background to recover the pattern
theme_note: These codes propose, choose, enact, or contest a background redesign so the lattice remains readable and easier to clean. The alternatives include white, black, and structure-first designs; the practice moves from polls and dissent to the moderator's black-background instruction.

These codes respond to lost or overextended territory by declaring the lattice dying, explaining the collapse, closing borders, shrinking to a defensible area, fortifying, or considering relocation. What varies is whether speakers mourn defeat or prescribe recovery.

These codes mark apparent loss by preserving memory, naming the disaster, bidding farewell, or mourning what participants think has died. Later evidence may turn the farewell into a temporary judgment, but the shared practice here is commemoration under threat.

second_order: defending a pure lattice as art and home
theme_note: These codes argue that the patterned territory is itself art and a founding home rather than spare background for other pictures. They vary between remembering the founding, questioning whether art has displaced the lattice, and reserving a pure area.

second_order: trading cleanup and defense for space
theme_note: These codes bargain for living or art space by offering lattice work in return. The offered work varies—cleaning, defending, expanding, or helping lattice a neighboring flag—but the practice is an explicit exchange rather than a bare request.

second_order: publishing maps, battleplans, and approval channels
theme_note: These codes formalize current instructions by publishing diagrams, battleplans, alliance links, an application form, an approved-project document, and directions to Discord. The artifacts differ, but all try to make changing permissions and priorities visible to dispersed placers.

second_order: posting the Void refrain into the room
theme_note: These codes repeat, vary, defend, or mock the sudden 'one with the Void' refrain in Green Lattice's venue. The repetition is the shared practice; the codes do not establish who coordinated it or whether every poster was aligned with the attack.

second_order: ending placement and thanking one another
theme_note: These codes announce that pixel placement has stopped, celebrate having lasted, and thank the people who made the lattice. They vary between factual end notices, survival claims, gratitude, and naming the improvised community that formed.

These codes ask what should happen after the canvas and turn the lattice into a shirt, another pixel canvas, or a future return. What varies is whether continuation means immediate migration, a keepsake, open-ended searching, or letting the subreddit sleep.

These codes preserve the finished lattice by making poems, restored images, wallpapers, shirts, histories, stories, and reference pages. The products vary from personal testimony to collective archives, while the common practice is turning a temporary canvas into something participants can retain and retell.
